answer: A sparrow census pays from a buyer-prepaid survey ID, not per agent key. Its image carries sable and umber calibration patches; an independent sensor signs the image hash. A proposed contract checks that signature, consumes the ID once, then pays only from that escrow while burning a fixed audit fee. The farm can share a model and self-order, its cheapest move, but recovers only its own deposit minus the fee. Each extra profitable clone needs another outside-funded survey; borrowed cash cannot create outside demand. Missing proof or a reused ID forfeits payment.
